name: Hudl: AI Video Analysis and Automated Capture Across Sport
title: Hudl: AI Video Analysis and Automated Capture Across Sport
answer: Hudl's website documents a product family that carries AI into everyday coaching work, from Focus auto-tracking cameras that film and upload games without an operator to Hudl IQ, which automatically identifies formations, routes, coverages and blitzes in American football. Coaches quoted in a Hudl blog describe AI handling basic film breakdown, building position-group playlists and linking data to film, while Statsbomb and Live Soccer Data supply event-level and real-time soccer analytics to professional teams.

sections.body: Hudl publishes this material on hudl.com, where it appears as a mix of product pages, a company about page and a blog post. The product pages cover Hudl Focus cameras, automated football camera systems, Hudl IQ, Hudl Statsbomb, Hudl Live Soccer Data and Balltime. The blog post reports a panel discussion with high school football coaches about AI, live replay and film study workflows. The pages describe current products and capabilities rather than dated research, and no publication dates are stated beyond the reading date of the site.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The Focus line consists of AI-powered auto-tracking cameras, including Focus Outdoor for stadiums, Focus Indoor for gyms and Focus Portable for teams filming away games or practice. The cameras start on time, follow the action using player tracking algorithms built for specific sports, and upload footage automatically, so all high school games in Focus-equipped stadiums reach the Hudl library whether played at home, away or at a neutral site. Professional analysts use the live feeds for live and collaborative coding, and programmes control livestream monetisation including pay-per-view. Hudl IQ applies AI, computer vision and data collectors to American football, automatically identifying every formation, route, coverage and blitz, tracking every player at 30 frames per second, and offering models such as expected completion, CPOE, CROE and EPA alongside pass placement and catch radius data. Statsbomb supplies soccer data across more than 40 key leagues, with models for expected goals, possession state, headers, defensive responsibility and expected pass, plus APIs and file formats for integration. Live Soccer Data delivers real-time events and player locations by API. Balltime brings AI tagging of every touch to individual volleyball athletes. In the blog post, coaches describe AI as an extension of the coach for reports and labelling, able to handle basic breakdown quickly, build position-group playlists and connect data to film for immediate delivery to players.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: Hudl IQ is said to deliver 10 times more data than any one provider and to track every player at 30 frames per second. Statsbomb event data is described as over 3,000 events per game and more than 50 additional metrics across 40 or more key leagues, with player locations and off-ball metrics derived from single camera footage across more than 120 competitions. Statsbomb provides player-location data for 40 or more key leagues at no extra cost. A coach on the panel said AI could let a programme either focus on coaching or spend the same ten hours per week going deeper into analysis, and another said a staff of four or five can still affect real change.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: This source shows how AI reaches the sideline in practice rather than in principle. The camera products remove the need for a dedicated operator and push film into a library automatically, while the analytics products turn that film into tagged events, models and position-specific clips. For a reader following AI in sport, the useful material is the described division of labour: machines handle capture, tagging, breakdown and data-to-film linking, and coaches spend their time on interpretation and teaching. The soccer data pages add a professional-team view of the same pipeline, with real-time feeds feeding modelling, broadcast graphics and proprietary systems.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Sports

sections.body: The material is published by Hudl about Hudl products, so claims about scale, accuracy and competitive advantage are the company's own and are not independently verified here. The blog post reports a small panel of high school football coaches, so its observations reflect that group rather than a broad survey. Coverage is weighted towards American football and soccer, with volleyball represented only by Balltime, and other sports are not addressed. No pricing, independent evaluation or dated research is given, and the pages describe capabilities without reporting measured outcomes.
